CHECK THE CONSUMER'S PREDICATE BEFORE GRINDING A HYPOTHESIS: the DD-R certificate gate was over-strong for ~7 sessions.

**TRIMMED 2026-07-27 (janitor hygiene pass, run 0048 round 5).** Two appended annotation layers had grown this item to roughly triple its useful length, and both restated `I-0360` rather than adding to the rule. The rule and its evidence are kept; the "what the relaxation does not buy" narrative now lives in one place. Do not grow this item again — file a new item and cross-reference.

**THE RULE (this is the durable part).** Before grinding a certificate/finiteness hypothesis in this project, check what the actual CONSUMER's predicate is. The project has both a global notion (`IsCertified`, over the whole chart ring $R_Z$) and a Zariski-local one (`IsLocallyCertified`, `DivisorFamilyZar.lean:71`), and **every** downstream interface was built on the local one: `divRepPullAt` (`DivRepAffKit.lean`), `DivRepAffinePullback.pull`, `divRepClassifyZar` (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:244`) all take `DivFamZar`, never `IsCertified` over $R$.

**WHAT WENT WRONG.** The lane attacked `(D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g` via `divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning(_degree)` (`DivSchemeCertUniv.lean:144`, `DivSchemeCertSeed.lean:61`). Its `hnoLeak` input is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (`I-0209`), so the lane sat blocked on an unprovable hypothesis that no consumer ever required.

**THE RELAXATION THAT LANDED** (commits `2709f44d9`, `b959b798b`, `612b5fae0`, `f868c9425`; files `Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean`, `DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`, `DivSchemeCertZarTube.lean`; all kernel-checked warning-free):

- `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` — span-top production rule.
- `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the POINTWISE gate, via quasi-compactness of $\operatorname{Spec} R$.
- `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` — the adaptation is free, so only the certificate over the shrunken base remains.
- `exists_basicOpen_supportTube` / `exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre` — the support tube refined to the basic-open (Away) shape the gate consumes.
- `isLocallyCertified_of_isCertified` — the old global gate is a special case, so this is a genuine weakening, not a parallel track.

Round 4 pushed it one interface further: `divRepPullAt` now takes a `DivFamZar` class per chart instead of a `CertifiedDivisorFamily` (commit `1e4ac5b52`), which is exactly what this item asked for.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY — read `I-0360`, do not re-derive here.** The relaxation does not unblock U1: the chart-confinement no-go is about PRODUCING a certificate, not consuming one, and `IsLocallyCertified` fails for exactly the divisors `IsCertified` fails for. For where the campaign gate actually sits, read `I-0365` (it is L8, local surjectivity, not U2). For the field-size boundary of the R1 escape, read `I-0346`.
==========I-0365==========
WHERE THE DD-R GATE ACTUALLY BITES: NOT U2, NOT 'the certificate for the universal family' -- IT IS L8, LOCAL SURJECTIVITY. Established run 0048 round 5 by a seven-front recon with an adversarial refuter per front; the refuter on the 'single gate' front overturned the recon on exactly this point, and I re-verified it at source.

THE OLD FRAMING, which several roadmap rows and worksheets still use: 'the divrep tail is
independent of the certificate; the certificate only gates U2'. That is FALSE, and the reason is
structural rather than a failed proof.

WHAT IS TRUE.
 * DivFamZar C S pi g is BY DEFINITION a quotient of LOCALLY CERTIFIED divisor families
   (DivisorFamilyZar.lean:224,:235). Certificates are not consumed by the tail -- they come with
   the object.
 * So on the consuming side certificates are free, and DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover
   (DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:433) is a landed THEOREM that produces a certified representative
   Zariski-locally from the vehicle itself. It is unfolded by every keystone of the classifier:
   DivRepClassifyZar.lean:128 (exists_isDivRepClassify), :176 (isDivRepClassify_unique),
   :230 (exists_overHom_isDivRepClassify), DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean:361 and :363
   (eq_of_isDivRepClassify).
 * IsDivRepClassify (DivRepClassifyZar.lean:90) universally quantifies over
   (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C T pi g) in its body at :95-97 -- a hypothesis, so scarcity of
   certificates makes the predicate EASIER, not harder.

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is the campaign's real shape. The no-go (DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:30-31,
:131) says DivFamZar is BLIND to connected divisors meeting both pinned fibres. So divFunctor
C pi g is a PROPER SUBFUNCTOR of 'degree-g relative divisors'. Representing it is not the problem

Abel map out of it is not Zariski-locally surjective, because the classes whose only witnesses
are the invisible divisors are not hit. That is L8, the
Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc f) input of pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:165), roadmap dat-b B-6.

    understood as WIDENING DivFamZar until it sees enough divisors for L8 to hold. Judge any
    proposed repair by that criterion, not by whether it makes a certificate easier to prove.
 3. Anyone proving L8 must check which functor the surjectivity is stated against. Local
    surjectivity onto Pic^0 from a subfunctor that misses classes is FALSE, not merely unproved,

**THE RULE (this is the durable part).** Before grinding a certificate/finiteness hypothesis in this project, check what the actual CONSUMER's predicate is. The project has both a global notion (`IsCertified`, over the whole chart ring $R_Z$) and a Zariski-local one (`IsLocallyCertified`, `DivisorFamilyZar.lean:71`), and **every** downstream interface was built on the local one: `divRepPullAt` (`DivRepAffKit.lean`), `DivRepAffinePullback.pull`, `divRepClassifyZar` (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:244`) all take `DivFamZar`, never `IsCertified` over $R$.

Its `hnoLeak` input is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (`I-0209`), so the lane sat blocked on an unprovable hypothesis that no consumer ever required.

- `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the POINTWISE gate, via quasi-compactness of $\operatorname{Spec} R$.

- `isLocallyCertified_of_isCertified` — the old global gate is a special case, so this is a genuine weakening, not a parallel track.

Round 4 pushed it one interface further: `divRepPullAt` now takes a `DivFamZar` class per chart instead of a `CertifiedDivisorFamily` (commit `1e4ac5b52`), which is exactly what this item asked for.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY — read `I-0360`, do not re-derive here.** The relaxation does not unblock U1: the chart-confinement no-go is about PRODUCING a certificate, not consuming one, and `IsLocallyCertified` fails for exactly the divisors `IsCertified` fails for. For where the campaign gate actually sits, read `I-0365` (it is L8, local surjectivity, not U2). For the field-size boundary of the R1 escape, read `I-0346`.
==========I-0365==========
WHERE THE DD-R GATE ACTUALLY BITES: NOT U2, NOT 'the certificate for the universal family' -- IT IS L8, LOCAL SURJECTIVITY. Established run 0048 round 5 by a seven-front recon with an adversarial refuter per front; the refuter on the 'single gate' front overturned the recon on exactly this point, and I re-verified it at source.

THE OLD FRAMING, which several roadmap rows and worksheets still use: 'the divrep tail is
independent of the certificate; the certificate only gates U2'. That is FALSE, and the reason is
structural rather than a failed proof.

WHAT IS TRUE.
 * DivFamZar C S pi g is BY DEFINITION a quotient of LOCALLY CERTIFIED divisor families
   (DivisorFamilyZar.lean:224,:235). Certificates are not consumed by the tail -- they come with
   the object.
 * So on the consuming side certificates are free, and DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover
   (DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:433) is a landed THEOREM that produces a certified representative
   Zariski-locally from the vehicle itself. It is unfolded by every keystone of the classifier:
   DivRepClassifyZar.lean:128 (exists_isDivRepClassify), :176 (isDivRepClassify_unique),
   :230 (exists_overHom_isDivRepClassify), DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean:361 and :363
   (eq_of_isDivRepClassify).
 * IsDivRepClassify (DivRepClassifyZar.lean:90) universally quantifies over
   (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C T pi g) in its body at :95-97 -- a hypothesis, so scarcity of
   certificates makes the predicate EASIER, not harder.

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is the campaign's real shape. The no-go (DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:30-31,
:131) says DivFamZar is BLIND to connected divisors meeting both pinned fibres. So divFunctor
C pi g is a PROPER SUBFUNCTOR of 'degree-g relative divisors'. Representing it is not the problem
-- the whole L9-L13 tail does that honestly, over a section variable, and round 5 nearly finished
it. The problem is that a representable but too-small divisor functor cannot cover Pic^0: the
Abel map out of it is not Zariski-locally surjective, because the classes whose only witnesses
are the invisible divisors are not hit. That is L8, the
Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc f) input of pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:165), roadmap dat-b B-6.

HOW TO APPLY.
 1. Stop describing U2 / the affine package as 'the gate'. They are tail work and they are nearly
    done. The gate is L8.
 2. Repairs R1 (twist by Aut(P^1)) and R2 (generalise FinCoverData's piece type) are correctly
    understood as WIDENING DivFamZar until it sees enough divisors for L8 to hold. Judge any
    proposed repair by that criterion, not by whether it makes a certificate easier to prove.
 3. Anyone proving L8 must check which functor the surjectivity is stated against. Local
    surjectivity onto Pic^0 from a subfunctor that misses classes is FALSE, not merely unproved,
    and no amount of work on the affine package changes it.

geometrically integral over `k` — `Scheme.HasRigidPushforward C` holds.

(`Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean`) fed by `rigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange_proved`
of §2.

This is the discharge `Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`'s class docstring anticipated; that
docstring has been corrected accordingly, and the class is kept rather than deleted so consumers
keep reading as hypotheses on the curve.  The `[HasRigidPushforward C]` binders on the three
extraction theorems now synthesize for an AJC curve, as §4 witnesses, and
`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Witness.lean` exhibits a curve satisfying the three hypotheses, so
neither this instance nor §4 is vacuous. -/
instance instHasRigidPushforwardOfCurve
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    Scheme.HasRigidPushforward C :=
  hasRigidPushforward_of_gammaBaseChange C
    (fun A _ _ _ => rigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange_proved C A)

/-! ## §4. The B3 headlines, unconditionally

The three extraction theorems of `Picard/RigidPushforward.lean` §3–§4 carry a
`[HasRigidPushforward C]` binder.  Restated here for an AJC curve *without* that binder — the
gate is synthesized by §3, not assumed.  These are the honest "the consumers synthesize"
witnesses: if §3 were absent, none of the three would elaborate. -/

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A]
variable (L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules)

/-- **B3 local freeness, unconditional.**  For an invertible `L` on `C_A` with fibrewise
`h¹ = 0` at all scheme points, `q_* L` is free of rank `h⁰(C_t, L_t)` near every `t : Spec A`. -/
